Start Here

NCode's look and feel is called Instrument. Its mark is a value held between the braces of code, and every NCode surface is built the same way: a neutral, precisely made case of engraved labels, keys and wells that holds live values, lit on screens and lamps, with the mark's own brace drawn around what one boundary holds.

This guide says what Instrument is made of, when to use each part, and which file in this repository carries it. The pages in specimens/ show every part at work: foundations.html holds the whole kit, and each other page is a scene from a real surface.

Principles

  1. The frame is fixed, the value is live. Structure is stone and engraved type. Color belongs to values, to state and to the tenant.
  2. A brace marks a scope. The mark's brace is drawn around what one boundary holds, and nowhere else.
  3. Names are engraved, values are displayed. A fixed part carries narrow capitals. Anything read off the system is monospace.
  4. Depth means one thing. A lip below: press it. A shade above: fill it. Flush: a plate. Hard edges only.
  5. State is lit, and said. A lamp or a lit plate always sits beside a word, and its shape changes with the state.
  6. Hazards wear tape. Test environments, cautions and the platform boundary carry amber and black stripes.
  7. Keys travel, readouts tick. A key moves 2 pixels in 70 milliseconds. A value changes in one step. Nothing else moves.

Which File for What

Every path is from the root of a release. Keep the release's folders side by side: css/base.css finds the braces in brace/, and css/fonts.css finds the fonts in fonts/.

You buildTake
A page in plain HTML and CSStokens/tokens.css, css/fonts.css with fonts/, css/base.css with brace/
A documentation site on Starlighttokens/tokens.css, css/fonts.css with fonts/, css/starlight.css
Code blocks highlighted by Expressive Codesyntax/instrument-screen.json, on a page that loads tokens/tokens.css
A Material UI applicationmui/instrument.json, tokens/tokens.mjs, tokens/derive.mjs, css/fonts.css with fonts/
A tool or a format with its own themetokens/tokens.json, in the Design Tokens format 2025.10, or tokens/tokens.resolver.json, with the two themes as a modifier
An emailemail/instrument.html, every value written inline
A page without 2024 CSStokens/tokens.static.css, every color written out
Slides in Marpslides/instrument.css, with fonts/OFL-Instrument-Sans.txt and fonts/OFL-Martian-Mono.txt
A logo in a README, a favicon, a package iconThe files in logo/ncode/, or logo/identity/ for NCode Identity, as Marks says
An iconicons/sprite.svg with css/base.css, or one icons/<name>.svg; icons/LICENSE-Lucide.txt with any Lucide icon, as Icons says
A component that draws the brace, an icon or the mark inlinebrace/brace.json, icons/icons.json, logo/ncode/outlines.json, logo/identity/outlines.json

Applying it says how, for each.

Tokens: the One Rule

Read semantic tokens: the color roles (--nc-color-*), the type roles (--nc-type-*), elevation, the font families, the measures and the two tenant inputs. The color ramps and the steps of the type scale are private primitives, which may change in any release (the decision).

Pin a Version

Take files from one tagged release's archive, whose build provenance the GitHub CLI verifies, and check them against its manifest.json: copy vendoring/vendor-brand.mjs into your repository, name the files you take in a brand.lock.json, and run it with --update <version> to verify and vendor them and with --check in your gate to prove they did not drift. Applying it has the steps, and Versions and license says what a version number promises.
